full_judgment:
Md. Abdur Rouf J: This appeal, following leave, by the pre-empties is from the judgment and order dated 18 February, 1992 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4127 of 1991, allowing pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, after setting aside the concurrent decisions of the courts below, which had refused pre-emption on the ground of limitation. 

 2. The pre-emptor's admitted co-sharers, viz Md. Anwar Hossain and Md. Abu Taher (who were opposite party Nos. 5 and 6 in the original pre-emption proceeding but have not been made parties in this appeal) had sold the land in question to the pre-emptee appellants by registered kabala dated 20 November, 1975. The pre-emptor on 8-11-78 instituted Misc Case No. 292 of 1978 in the Court of Munsif, First Court, Kushtia claiming pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the case on being renumbered as Misc Case No. 4 of 1983 was tried by the Court of Munsif, Kumarkhali. The pre-emptor alleged that she came to know of the sale for the first time on 16 September, 1978 from one Tajuddin (PW 2) and that she had no scope of knowing about the sale earlier as the land in question had all along been in possession of the pre-empties as bargaders under the sellers since before their purchase. 

 5. Mr. Sharifuddin Chaklader, learned Advocate-on-Record for the appellant, submits that PW 2 having not appeared in court for cross-examination by the pre-emptee, his statements, made in the examination-in-chief on commission, got no evidentiary value and, as such, the learned Judge of the High Court Division erred in law in taking into consideration his inadmissible evidence in reversing the concurrent finding of the courts below. 

 8. Sub-section (1) of section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 provides that when a raiyat dies intestate leaving no heir entitled to inherit under the law of inheritance to which he is subject, the interest of such a raiyat in a holding shall be extinguished and under sub-section (2) thereof, the Revenue Officer may enter on the holding ; and the holding shall, with effect from the date on which the Revenue Officer so enters on it, vest absolutely in the Government free from all encumbrances, except the encumbrances on the holding which is extinguished under clause (a) of sub-section (1) thereof. 

 For the reasons stated above we do not find any substance in this appeal. It is therefore, dismissed without any order as to costs.
